title: The Model Code of Conduct

endcard.line: Pictures: Christian Haugen from Trondheim, Norway (CC BY 2.0); Daderot (public domain)

anim.title: 16 March 2024
items: The Model Code of Conduct comes into effect

segments.say: On the sixteenth of March twenty twenty-four, the Election Commission announced the Lok Sabha election schedule. That same day, the Model Code of Conduct came into effect.
The code is meant to keep a level playing field, so that those in office can't use it to tilt an election.
The code begins when the schedule is announced, and ends once the election process is complete.

anim.title: Who it binds
items: The Central Government, for announcements about those States

segments.say: It binds parties and candidates. It also covers the Central Government's announcements and policy decisions for the States going to the polls.
The Election Commission enforces it by directing officials, from Chief Secretaries to district officers.

anim.below: of cVIGIL complaints resolved in under 100 minutes (first month, 2024)

segments.say: Citizens can report violations on the cVIGIL app. In that first month, about two lakh sixty-eight thousand complaints came in, and ninety-two per cent were resolved in under a hundred minutes.
For GS Two, remember the window: from the announcement of the schedule until the election is complete. And remember that it reaches the Central Government too.

sources: PIB, ECI states position on enforcement of MCC during first month (PRID 2018017): Model Code came into effect on 16 March 2024 with the announcement of the general elections; level playing field; 2,68,080 complaints on cVIGIL, action in 2,67,762, 92% resolved in an average of less than 100 minutes; DMs, DEOs and SPs sensitised to enforce the code

PIB, 16 March 2026 (PRID 2240566): with the announcement of the schedule, ECI directed Chief Secretaries and CEOs on the immediate coming into force of the MCC; the MCC also applies to the Central Government for announcements and policy decisions for the States/UT concerned
PIB, 7 May 2026 (PRID 2258673): MCC ceases to be in operation in the States/UTs that voted, except one assembly constituency

quiz.q: When does the Model Code of Conduct come into force?
options: Six months before the term ends
When the Election Commission announces the schedule
quiz.why: PIB: it came into effect with the announcement of the schedule.

quiz.q: Does the Model Code apply to the Central Government during State elections?
options: Yes, for announcements about the poll-bound States
quiz.why: PIB, March 2026: it applies to the Centre's announcements and policy decisions for those States.

options: An app for citizens to report code violations
quiz.why: PIB: complaints on violations were filed by citizens on cVIGIL.

The script does not name the 1960s origins of the code or its legal status, because no official page with those was read. The opening card's date is the 2024 Lok Sabha announcement. Pictures have no faces and no party symbols. Moving facts: cVIGIL figures are from 2024 and will be replaced by newer ones.
